S-001.threat: External entity identity spoofing — attacker impersonates a legitimate external entity
S-001.cause: No authentication mechanism enforced for external entities
S-001.attack: Attacker crafts requests that appear to originate from a legitimate external entity

S-002.threat: Process identity spoofing — attacker impersonates a legitimate process
S-002.cause: Insufficient process authentication — callers are not required to prove their identity
S-002.attack: Attacker injects requests pretending to be a legitimate caller

S-003.threat: Session hijacking — attacker takes over an authenticated process session
S-003.cause: Weak session management — session tokens are predictable or transmitted insecurely
S-003.attack: Attacker captures or predicts a valid session token and impersonates a legitimate user

S-004.threat: Credential stuffing — attacker uses leaked credentials to authenticate
S-004.cause: No brute-force protection or multi-factor authentication
S-004.attack: Attacker uses breached credentials to authenticate against the process

S-005.threat: System identity spoofing — attacker impersonates the system or one of its components
S-005.cause: No system-level authentication — the system does not verify the identity of communicating peers
S-005.attack: Attacker sets up a rogue system claiming to be a legitimate component
